questions.question:
Seven boxes, A, B, C, D, E, F and G, are kept one over the other, but not necessarily in the same order.

Only three boxes are kept above G. Only one box is kept between B and G. Only three boxes are kept between B and C. C is kept at some place above G. F is kept immediately below C. E is kept at one of the places above D. A is not kept immediately above or below B.

How many boxes are kept below E?
questions.solution:
Given: Seven boxes C, F, J, N, Q, S and V are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order.

Only three boxes are kept above G.

Only one box is kept between B and G.

Only three boxes are kept between B and C.

C is kept at some place above G.

F is kept immediately below C.

E is kept at one of the places above D.

A is not kept immediately above or below B.

 
 

 Positio

questions.question: Nayan starts from Point A and drives 45 km towards the north. He then takes a right turn, drives 37 km, turns right and drives 60 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 56 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 15 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only unless specified.)
questions.solution:
Given:

Nayan drives 45 km North.

He turns right → 37 km East.

He turns right → 60 km South.

He turns right → 56 km West.

He turns right → 15 km North and reaches point P.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5fd4af860b6212aadef69aed7b219653ab869864c129e2aae7dcad7e0eead788.png] 

Therefore, to reach Point A again, Nayan must drive 19 km towards the East.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

questions.question: Six people, A, B, C, D, E and F, are sitting in a row, facing north. A sits to the immediate right of E. B sits fourth to the left of E. Only one person sits between B and F. C sits to the immediate left of F. D sits second to the left of A. Three of the following four are alike in a certain way based on the given arrangement and thus form a group. Which is the one that does NOT belong to that group?
questions.solution:
Given: Six people A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting in a row facing north.

B sits fourth to the left of E.

A sits to the immediate right of E.

Only one person sits between B and F.

C sits to the immediate left of F.

D sits second to the left of A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/84e2795eec1127ef917f13683050d1f37f49382e88fe5e5c3afe7f67756f124a.png] 

Now, check the pairs:

Option 1) FD → D is to the immediate right of F 

Option 2) BA → A is not to the immediate right of B 

Option 3) DE → E is to the immediate right of D 

Option 4) CF → F is to the immediate right of C 

Thus, three pairs follow the pattern “second person is immediate right of first person”, except BA.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All tables are golds.

No table is a helmet.

**Conclusions:**

(I): Some helmets are golds.

(II): All golds are helmets.
questions.solution:
Given Statements:

All tables are golds.

No table is a helmet.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/afcb8dfd660dfa21e0b6cb053444e49bc5ddd34dcd97405775b81b5b3e9a96f0.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some helmets are golds – Does not follow (No definite relation is given).

II. All golds are helmets – Does not follow (Tables are golds, but no table is a helmet).

So, neither conclusion I nor II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 2.**
